extracted.intended_audience: researchers and developers working on federated learning simulation and evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for selecting, building, and evaluating software and datasets for federated learning research simulations, including required simulation capabilities and evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Efficient processing of partitioned datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Simulations of federated learning require dealing with multiple issues that do not arise in datacenter ML research, for example, efficiently processing partitioned datasets, with computations running on different simulated devices, each with a variable amount of data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should handle datasets partitioned across many simulated devices and support per-device computation where devices may hold widely varying amounts of data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication-cost metrics (bytes uploaded/downloaded)
rubrics_metrics.description: FL research also requires different metrics such as the number of bytes upload or downloaded by device.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track per-device and aggregate communication (upload/download) to evaluate communication efficiency of algorithms and protocols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simulation of time-varying client arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to simulate issues like time-varying arrival of different clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simulators should model clients that become available/unavailable over time to reflect realistic participation patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modeling client drop-out correlated with local data
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to simulate client drop-out that is potentially correlated with the nature of the local dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support non-random dropout scenarios where dropout probability depends on client data characteristics, since this can materially affect learning and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large-scale simulation capabilities and flexible orchestration
rubrics_metrics.description: TensorFlow Federated specifically targets research use cases, providing large-scale simulation capabilities as well as flexible orchestration for the control of sampling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer frameworks that scale to many simulated devices and provide orchestration primitives to control client sampling strategies during experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-platform support (on-device, distributed, single-machine)
rubrics_metrics.description: FedML is a research-oriented library. It supports three platforms: on-device training for IoT and mobile devices, distributed computing, and single-machine simulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose tools that allow experiments in realistic on-device settings, as well as scalable distributed and reproducible single-machine simulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm, model, and dataset diversity support
rubrics_metrics.description: For research diversity, FedML also supports various algorithms (e.g., decentralized learning, vertical FL, and split learning), models, and datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks should make it easy to experiment with different FL variants, model architectures, and datasets to evaluate robustness and generality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy-preserving training primitives (federated learning, DP, MPC)
rubrics_metrics.description: PySyft is a Python library for secure, private Deep Learning. PySyft decouples private data from model training, using federated learning, differential privacy, and multi-party computation (MPC) within PyTorch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When privacy is a goal, prefer frameworks that integrate federated training with differential privacy and MPC tooling to enable experiments with realistic privacy protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of datasets plus simulation and evaluation capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaf provides multiple datasets (see below), as well as simulation and evaluation capabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks that bundle standard federated datasets and evaluation utilities reduce engineering overhead and improve comparability across studies.
